boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Mount Holyoke College
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food destinations with published late hours in the South Hadley–Pioneer Valley area.

cards.title: Ebenezer’s Bar & Grill
cards.subtitle: 60 Bridge Street, South Hadley
cards.notes: Check the kitchen timing before leaving: the business lists food service until 10 p.m., while Friday and Saturday hours run to midnight.
cards.short_summary: A South Hadley Falls option with explicitly listed evening kitchen service.
cards.evidence_claim: Ebenezer’s lists kitchen hours until 10 p.m. and Friday–Saturday business hours until midnight.
cards.access_notes: Food service is listed until 10 p.m.; Friday and Saturday business hours are 11 a.m.–midnight.

cards.title: Campus Pizza
cards.subtitle: 150 Fearing Street, Amherst
cards.notes: Use the posted Thursday–Saturday window for a late pickup; the restaurant lists those nights from 5 p.m. until 2 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A pizza-and-calzone stop with a published 2 a.m. weekend closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Pizza lists Thursday–Saturday hours of 5 p.m.–2 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Open Thursday–Saturday 5 p.m.–2 a.m.; Sunday 4–9 p.m. and Wednesday 5–10 p.m.; closed Monday–Tuesday.

cards.title: Chicken & Co. @ Southwest
cards.subtitle: Hampden Building, 141 Southwest Circle, Amherst
cards.notes: Plan this as a Tuesday–Saturday destination: UMass Dining posts a 7 p.m.–2 a.m. schedule and accepts cash and credit cards.
cards.short_summary: A university dining location with published service through 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Dining lists Chicken & Co. @ Southwest open Tuesday–Saturday from 7 p.m.–2 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Tuesday–Saturday, 7 p.m.–2 a.m. The official page lists cash, credit cards, UCard, Dining Dollars, and YCMP.

cards.title: Sweets and More
cards.subtitle: Field Hall, 171 Orchard Hill Drive, Amherst
cards.notes: For a later sweet or snack, use the posted Monday–Thursday and Sunday schedule; the location is identified on the official dining page.
cards.short_summary: A student-run UMass food business with published 11:30 p.m. hours.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Dining lists Sweets and More open Monday–Thursday and Sunday from 7:30 a.m.–11:30 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours are Monday–Thursday and Sunday, 7:30 a.m.–11:30 p.m.; payment methods listed include cash and credit cards.

cards.title: Procrastination Station
cards.subtitle: W.E.B. Du Bois Library, 154 Hicks Way, Amherst
cards.notes: Use the Monday–Thursday regular schedule for a late library stop; verify seasonal hours, which the official page lists separately from regular hours.
cards.short_summary: A library café with regular-hours service until 10 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Dining lists Procrastination Station’s regular Monday–Thursday hours as 8 a.m.–10 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Regular Monday–Thursday hours are 8 a.m.–10 p.m.; the page also posts different summer hours.

cards.title: Wendy’s in Hadley
cards.subtitle: 376 Russell Street, Hadley
cards.notes: This is a practical late-drive option: the official location page publishes restaurant and drive-thru hours through 3 a.m. every day.
cards.short_summary: A Hadley restaurant with consistently published 3 a.m. closing times.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s lists this Hadley restaurant and drive-thru open 10 a.m.–3 a.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and drive-thru hours are listed as 10 a.m.–3 a.m. Monday through Sunday.

cards.title: Taco Bell in Hadley
cards.subtitle: 348 Russell Street, Hadley
cards.notes: Check whether you need drive-thru or dine-in before heading out: the official page separately lists each service’s hours, including late drive-thru service.
cards.short_summary: A Hadley location with drive-thru hours extending as late as 3 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists this location’s drive-thru open until 2 a.m. most nights and until 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru closes 2 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; dine-in hours are separately posted.

cards.title: Taco Bell in Holyoke
cards.subtitle: 2199 Northampton Street, Holyoke
cards.notes: For a later Holyoke option, follow the official location schedule and confirm the service mode; drive-thru hours extend later than posted dine-in hours.
cards.short_summary: A Holyoke location with published drive-thru service through 2 or 3 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists this Holyoke location’s drive-thru open until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru closes at 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday; dine-in hours are separately posted.

cards.title: Taco Bell in Northampton
cards.subtitle: 203 King Street, Northampton
cards.notes: This farther regional option posts overnight drive-thru hours; confirm the day before traveling because closing time differs by day of week.
cards.short_summary: A Northampton location with official drive-thru hours as late as 5 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours until 3 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 5 a.m. Thursday–Saturday at this Northampton location.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru closes 3 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 5 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; the official page lists dine-in hours separately.

cards.entity_name: Taco Bell / Pizza Hut — 1471 Memorial Drive
cards.title: Taco Bell / Pizza Hut in Chicopee
cards.subtitle: 1471 Memorial Drive, Chicopee
cards.notes: Use the official location listing when planning a longer regional run: it publishes daily drive-thru service until 3 a.m. and dine-in until 2 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A Chicopee co-branded location with published overnight service.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists this Chicopee location’s drive-thru open daily until 3 a.m. and dine-in until 2 a.m.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell / Pizza Hut — 1471 Memorial Drive, Chicopee
cards.access_notes: Officially listed drive-thru hours are 7 a.m.–3 a.m. daily; dine-in hours are 7 a.m.–2 a.m. daily.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus places for studying, making, gathering and participating in college life, supported by current Mount Holyoke sources.

cards.title: Settle into the Williston Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Level 4, Williston Library / LITS Complex
cards.notes: Bring a laptop, a book or a small group; use the quiet-zone seating and nearby computers for focused work between classes.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, flexible library room for individual work or small-group study.
cards.evidence_claim: LITS describes the Reading Room as suitable for reading, laptop or LITS-computer work, and small quiet group work.
cards.access_notes: Wheelchair accessible; listed as a quiet zone and not reservable.

cards.title: Use the Information Commons for collaborative work
cards.subtitle: North Level 4, Williston Library / LITS Complex
cards.notes: Choose this talk-zone space when your work needs computers, printing nearby, soft seating or conversation that would not suit a quiet floor.
cards.short_summary: A library study area equipped for conversation, computers and printing.
cards.evidence_claim: LITS lists the Information Commons as a wheelchair-accessible talk zone with computers, nearby printing and soft seating.
cards.access_notes: Located on North Level 4 of Williston Library.

cards.title: Study or listen at Pratt Music Library
cards.subtitle: Ground floor, Pratt Music Hall
cards.notes: Work in the naturally lit reading room, consult scores and recordings, or use the small group listening-and-study room for music projects.
cards.short_summary: A music-focused library with study space, workstations and listening resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt Music Library offers study space, computer workstations, a small group listening and study room, and music materials.
cards.access_notes: The page lists the library on the ground floor of Pratt Music Hall; check LITS hours before visiting.

cards.title: Meet at the Language & Culture Commons
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Ciruti Language Center
cards.notes: Use the lounge for language-focused work or meet around a reservable LCC study room when you need computers and a quieter setup.
cards.short_summary: A language-and-culture resource space with a lounge and reservable study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: LITS identifies the Language & Culture Commons in Ciruti and lists wheelchair-accessible, reservable LCC study rooms with computers and nearby printing.
cards.access_notes: The LCC lounge is additionally open whenever Ciruti Language Center is open.

cards.title: Pause or work in the Kendade atrium
cards.subtitle: Kendade Hall, Science Center
cards.notes: Use the atrium for a study break, a conversation with friends or group-project time as you move through the Science Center complex.
cards.short_summary: A central science-building atrium designed for studying and informal time with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke describes the Kendade atrium as a space to study or hang out with friends and notes circular rooms for group projects.
cards.access_notes: Part of Kendade Hall in the Science Center complex.

cards.title: Use Blanchard Hall as a campus meeting point
cards.subtitle: Community Center
cards.notes: Meet up in the central atrium or choose its informal seating when you want to socialize, study or connect with Student Life services.
cards.short_summary: A three-level community hub with informal social and study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke describes Blanchard Hall’s entry level as the campus living room, with informal spaces for socializing and study.
cards.access_notes: The building also houses Student Life services; some rooms and activities may require reservation.

cards.title: Gather at the Unity Center
cards.subtitle: Room 206, Blanchard Hall
cards.notes: Attend an Intergroup Dialogue, connect with an affiliated student group or use the space for a conversation that welcomes differing experiences.
cards.short_summary: A Blanchard gathering space supporting dialogue, student organizations and community connection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Unity Center hosts most Intergroup Dialogues and is home to several student groups and peer-education programs.
cards.access_notes: Located at 206 Blanchard Hall; programming and access vary by activity.

cards.title: Make a project in the Fimbel Lab
cards.subtitle: Prospect Hall
cards.notes: Bring an academic or personal project, then use the lab’s tools and staff support to prototype, build or learn alongside other makers.
cards.short_summary: An 8,000-square-foot makerspace for projects, workshops and interdisciplinary collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fimbel Lab is open to the Mount Holyoke community for academic and personal projects and provides tools, people and resources for maker culture.
cards.source_title: Fimbel Maker & Innovation Lab | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: Open to the Mount Holyoke community, including Five College students taking Mount Holyoke classes; academic projects receive priority.

cards.title: Visit the living collection at Talcott Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: Mount Holyoke College Botanic Garden
cards.notes: Walk through the greenhouse collection to observe plants from different climates, or use a casual visit as a reset during a campus day.
cards.short_summary: A teaching greenhouse with tropical, subtropical and other non-hardy plants.
cards.evidence_claim: Talcott Greenhouse houses the Botanic Garden’s non-hardy plant collection and supports teaching across academic departments and programs.
cards.access_notes: Officially listed hours are Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–4 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday 1–4 p.m.

cards.title: Find the Gettell Amphitheater
cards.subtitle: Campus amphitheater
cards.notes: Use the grassy seating as a landmark during major college gatherings, and check the events calendar when Convocation or other programming is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor amphitheater used for Convocation and other documented campus traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke schedules Convocation in Gettell Amphitheater and identifies it as the setting for the college’s Convocation tradition.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor venue; event availability and arrangements vary by the college calendar.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-cost ways to spend time around Mount Holyoke College and South Hadley.

cards.title: Walk the Buttery Brook trail
cards.subtitle: Buttery Brook Park, South Hadley
cards.notes: Meet at the park and take an unhurried loop on the walking trail; use the benches for a conversation break before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A simple outdoor walk with room to linger.
cards.evidence_claim: South Hadley lists Buttery Brook Park’s walking trail among park amenities, and its general use is listed as free.
cards.source_title: Buttery Brook Park | South Hadley, MA
cards.access_notes: Use the park’s posted rules and seasonal conditions; general park use is listed as free.

cards.entity_name: Buttery Brook Park Disc Golf Course
cards.title: Bring discs for a casual round
cards.subtitle: Buttery Brook Park, South Hadley
cards.notes: Bring discs you already have and play a low-key round on the park’s disc golf course; keep the pace friendly for mixed skill levels.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission outdoor game when you bring your own gear.
cards.evidence_claim: South Hadley identifies a disc golf course at Buttery Brook Park and lists general park use as free.
cards.source_title: Buttery Brook Park | South Hadley, MA
cards.access_notes: Bring your own discs; do not reserve a rental facility. General park use is listed as free.

cards.entity_name: Buttery Brook Park Free Friday Night Concerts
cards.title: Catch a Friday bandshell concert
cards.subtitle: Buttery Brook Park bandshell, South Hadley
cards.notes: Bring a folding chair or blanket and listen at the bandshell. Food is available nearby, but attending the concert itself does not require a purchase.
cards.short_summary: A free summer music series at the park bandshell.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town describes its 2026 Friday night bandshell concert series as free, running May 15 through September 11 except July 3.
cards.source_title: Buttery Brook Park | South Hadley, MA
cards.access_notes: Scheduled Fridays, 5:00–7:30 p.m., through September 11, 2026; check for weather cancellations. Food and drinks are optional purchases.

cards.entity_name: Buttery Brook Park Friday Cruise Nights
cards.title: See the Friday Cruise Nights cars
cards.subtitle: Buttery Brook Park, South Hadley
cards.notes: Stroll the displayed vintage vehicles with friends and pair it with the live music if it is running; skip the optional food and beverage vendors.
cards.short_summary: A free weekly vintage-vehicle viewing night.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town invites the public to see the weekly vintage vehicles at Buttery Brook Park’s Cruise Nights, with admission free.
cards.source_title: Buttery Brook Park | South Hadley, MA
cards.access_notes: Scheduled Fridays, 5:00–7:30 p.m., May 15–September 11, 2026, except July 3; check for cancellations. Vendors are optional.

cards.title: Claim a picnic-table conversation spot
cards.subtitle: Buttery Brook Park, South Hadley
cards.notes: Use one of the park’s picnic tables for a read-aloud, cards you already own, or a long catch-up; leave the table clear for the next group.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor table hang without booking a pavilion.
cards.evidence_claim: South Hadley lists picnic tables and seating areas at Buttery Brook Park, while the park’s general use is listed as free.
cards.source_title: Buttery Brook Park | South Hadley, MA
cards.access_notes: Use unreserved general-use seating; pavilions and the log cabin are separate rental facilities.

cards.title: Find the Verdance sculpture
cards.subtitle: Buttery Brook Park, between pickleball parking and the playground
cards.notes: Take a short park walk to the sculpture, compare details from different angles, and use it as a clear meeting point before another park activity.
cards.short_summary: A named public artwork to seek out in the park.
cards.evidence_claim: South Hadley’s Buttery Brook Park reopening information identifies the new sculpture “Verdance” between pickleball parking and the playground; general park use is free.
cards.source_title: Buttery Brook Park Grand Reopening Event Details and Map
cards.access_notes: View it during normal park access and do not climb on the artwork or enter reserved facilities.

cards.title: Meet beside the playground
cards.subtitle: Buttery Brook Park, South Hadley
cards.notes: Use the open playground area as a daytime meeting point, then walk the park or settle at nearby seating; keep the space welcoming for families.
cards.short_summary: A straightforward outdoor rendezvous point in the park.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town’s reopening information identifies a playground at Buttery Brook Park, and the Town lists general park use as free.
cards.source_title: Buttery Brook Park | South Hadley, MA
cards.access_notes: Use during general park hours and follow posted park rules; do not use reserved rental areas.

cards.entity_name: Mount Holyoke Range State Park Hiking
cards.title: Hike the Mount Holyoke Range
cards.subtitle: Mount Holyoke Range State Park, nearby Amherst and Granby
cards.notes: Choose a marked trail that fits the group’s experience, share the trail map before leaving, and turn back early if weather or daylight changes.
cards.short_summary: Thirty-plus miles of marked trails near South Hadley.
cards.evidence_claim: Massachusetts DCR says Mount Holyoke Range State Park has more than 30 miles of blazed trails and free parking at the Notch Visitor Center.
cards.source_title: Mount Holyoke Range State Park | Mass.gov
cards.access_notes: Open sunrise to sunset. Use marked trails, bring water, and follow DCR restrictions; parking at the Notch Visitor Center is free.

cards.title: Sit quietly in Abbey Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: Mount Holyoke College campus
cards.notes: When the chapel is not in use, meet for a quiet reset, journal for a few minutes, or sit together respectfully before continuing your day.
cards.short_summary: A campus space for a calm, no-cost pause.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke says visitors may sit, pray, meditate, or rest in Abbey Memorial Chapel when it is not in use.
cards.source_title: Quiet, Contemplative and Spiritual Places on Campus | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: Enter only when the chapel is not in use and respect services, ceremonies, and posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Pause at Wa-shin-an
cards.subtitle: Mount Holyoke College campus
cards.notes: Visit during the listed open period, move quietly through the space, and make it a short reflection stop with a friend or a solo reset.
cards.short_summary: A contemplative campus destination open beyond the college community.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke states that Wa-shin-an is open to the campus community and general public on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays from 1–5 p.m. during the academic year.
cards.source_title: Quiet, Contemplative and Spiritual Places on Campus | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: Academic-year access is Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, 1–5 p.m.; follow campus guidance and the space’s contemplative purpose.

warnings: The Mount Holyoke College Art Museum is currently closed for renovation until fall 2026, so it was not included despite its free admission.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named College Street destinations beside Mount Holyoke, each with a distinct stop to make.

cards.title: Browse the independent bookstore
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Village Commons
cards.notes: Cross College Street to the Village Commons and browse Odyssey’s shelves; Mount Holyoke identifies it as a nearby independent bookstore.
cards.short_summary: A book-focused stop directly across the corridor from campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke College identifies Odyssey Bookshop as an independent bookstore in the nearby Village Commons.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Village Commons beside the College Street corridor.

cards.title: See what’s playing
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Village Commons
cards.notes: Use the College Street side of the Village Commons for a movie-theater stop; the Commons identifies Tower Theaters among its tenants.
cards.short_summary: A cinema destination on the off-campus Commons side of College Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Village Commons identifies South Hadley's Tower Theaters and describes two first-run movie theatres on-site.
cards.access_notes: The Village Commons lists its address as 17 College Street, South Hadley.

cards.title: Look for a gift-shop browse
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — 25 College Street
cards.notes: Walk to 25 College Street and browse Arts Unlimited’s gift-shop offerings, a clearly signed destination within the Village Commons area.
cards.short_summary: A small retail stop with a direct College Street address.
cards.evidence_claim: Arts Unlimited describes itself as a gift shop and lists its address as 25 College St #6, South Hadley.
cards.access_notes: Business site lists 25 College St #6, South Hadley.

cards.title: Plan an ice-cream stop
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Village Commons
cards.notes: Head across College Street for Batch Ice Cream, which Mount Holyoke names as one of the Village Commons’ nearby restaurant options.
cards.short_summary: An ice-cream destination in the campus-adjacent commercial cluster.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke College lists Batch Ice Cream among restaurants in the Village Commons and pictures it there.
cards.access_notes: Mount Holyoke describes the Village Commons as across the street from campus.

cards.title: Choose a noodle or sushi meal
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Village Commons
cards.notes: Use the Village Commons storefront for IYA Sushi and Noodle Kitchen when you want a documented off-campus meal stop near College Street.
cards.short_summary: A named sushi-and-noodle restaurant in the Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke College identifies IYA Sushi and Noodle Kitchen as being in the Village Commons in South Hadley.
cards.access_notes: Mount Holyoke places it in the Village Commons just off campus.

cards.title: Spot a Village Commons restaurant
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Village Commons
cards.notes: Walk the Village Commons on the College Street side and use Kiao WanThai as a named, visually identifiable restaurant destination.
cards.short_summary: A documented food-and-entertainment tenant beside the College Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Village Commons includes Kiao WanThai among the businesses displayed in its current tenant images.
cards.access_notes: The Village Commons lists 17 College Street as its South Hadley address.

cards.title: Make a wellness appointment
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Village Commons
cards.notes: Use the College Street Village Commons walk to find Serenity, a distinct storefront documented by the Commons’ current tenant display.
cards.short_summary: A wellness-oriented storefront in the campus-adjacent Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Village Commons includes Serenity among the businesses displayed in its current tenant images.
cards.access_notes: The Village Commons is listed at 17 College Street, steps from Mount Holyoke College.

cards.title: Find a personal-care storefront
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Village Commons
cards.notes: Walk the Village Commons’ College Street frontage and locate Ochoa Hair, a named storefront in the complex’s current tenant display.
cards.short_summary: A distinct personal-care destination in the College Street commercial cluster.
cards.evidence_claim: The Village Commons includes Ochoa Hair among the businesses displayed in its current tenant images.
cards.access_notes: The Village Commons lists 17 College Street as its South Hadley address.

cards.title: Use the branch library
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — 47 College Street
cards.notes: Continue along College Street to Gaylord Memorial Library for a quieter civic destination within South Hadley’s two-library public system.
cards.short_summary: A public-library branch with a verified College Street address.
cards.evidence_claim: South Hadley identifies Gaylord Memorial Library as a branch of its public-library system at 47 College Street.
cards.access_notes: Town page lists the branch at 47 College Street and publishes its hours.

cards.title: Pause at the Town Common
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — at Hadley and Woodbridge streets
cards.notes: Walk to the Town Common on College Street for an outdoor civic landmark opposite the Village Commons and near Mount Holyoke’s entrance.
cards.short_summary: A named public common that anchors the College Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: South Hadley lists Town Common as a town facility on College Street and identifies its location at Hadley and Woodbridge streets.
cards.access_notes: Town facility page identifies the site as Town Common, College Street, South Hadley.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Mount Holyoke College rituals and class traditions, from the surprise Mountain Day bell to commencement’s laurel chains.

cards.title: Mountain Day
cards.subtitle: An unscheduled day off and trip to Mount Holyoke’s Summit House
cards.notes: Watch for the 7 a.m. bell announcement, then join the College’s day off by hiking or riding to the Summit House and taking in the view.
cards.short_summary: Mount Holyoke’s oldest tradition pauses classes for a community trip to the nearby mountain.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke says Mountain Day began in spring 1838; classes and obligations are cancelled and students are invited to the Summit House atop Mount Holyoke.
cards.access_notes: Timing is intentionally unscheduled; the College announces the day with the clock-tower bell.

cards.title: Laurel Parade
cards.subtitle: Commencement weekend procession to Mary Lyon’s grave
cards.notes: During Commencement weekend, watch seniors process four across with the laurel chains, then see the chain raised over Mary Lyon’s grave enclosure.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors carry linked laurel chains in a ritual connecting them with generations of Mount Holyoke alums.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke documents that seniors process with two 275-yard laurel chains to Mary Lyon’s grave, a tradition using laurel chains since 1902.
cards.access_notes: Held during Commencement weekend; participation details vary by graduating class and alum status.

cards.title: Pangy Day
cards.subtitle: Spring celebration of the “total world of women”
cards.notes: Look for the class-board programming near the final Friday of spring classes, and treat it as a campus event rather than a drop-in public festival.
cards.short_summary: Pangy Day is Mount Holyoke’s spring tradition of celebrating the “total world of women.”
cards.evidence_claim: The College states that Pangynaskeia, now commonly called Pangy Day, debuted in 1980 and is typically held on the last Friday of spring-semester classes.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Annual Events | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: Typically held on the last Friday of classes in the spring semester.

cards.title: M&Cs
cards.subtitle: Resident study-break snack and social gathering
cards.notes: If you live on campus, use the evening snack as a brief study break and a chance to meet neighbors in your residence hall.
cards.short_summary: M&Cs is the College’s recurring milk-and-cookies study-break tradition for resident students.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke identifies M&Cs as a long-standing College tradition: a light snack and social study break provided each evening for resident students.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Annual Events | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: The College describes M&Cs as serving resident students; check residence-life communications for current arrangements.

cards.title: Annual Vespers Concert
cards.subtitle: December holiday concert in Abbey Chapel
cards.notes: Check the College calendar as December approaches, then arrive with time to settle in for the annual holiday performance in Abbey Chapel.
cards.short_summary: A December campus concert tradition held in some form since 1899.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke states that its annual vespers concert has been held in some form every December since 1899 and reliably fills Abbey Chapel.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Annual Events | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: Held in December; confirm the current program, date, and attendance arrangements with the College.

cards.title: Convocation
cards.subtitle: Opening ritual for a new academic year
cards.notes: Attend at the start of the academic year to see class spirit and class identifiers displayed together in a formal campus gathering.
cards.short_summary: Convocation opens the academic year and foregrounds Mount Holyoke class spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke identifies Convocation as the tradition that kicks off the new academic year and brings class spirit into focus.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Annual Events | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: Scheduled at the beginning of the academic year; consult current College announcements for details.

cards.title: Big/Little Program
cards.subtitle: Junior and incoming first-year class pairing
cards.notes: If eligible, follow class-board sign-up guidance to connect with a junior “Big” or welcome an incoming first-year as a “Little.”
cards.short_summary: An early-1900s Mount Holyoke class tradition that pairs juniors with incoming first-year students.
cards.evidence_claim: The College states that the Big/Little program traces to the early 1900s and pairs a junior “Big” with an incoming first-year “Little.”
cards.source_title: Student Life and Engagement | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: Participation is organized through class boards and is intended for the paired student classes.

cards.title: DisOrientation
cards.subtitle: Senior and first-year class camaraderie ritual
cards.notes: Follow your class board’s instructions if participating; the current form is designed as a shared class experience, not an invitation to recreate older practices.
cards.short_summary: DisOrientation is a changing Mount Holyoke tradition connecting seniors and first-year students.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke describes DisOrientation as an ever-evolving tradition whose core purpose is building camaraderie between seniors and first-year students.
cards.source_title: Student Life and Engagement | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: Arrangements are class-board led and may change; use current student communications for participation details.

cards.title: Elfing
cards.subtitle: First-year and sophomore door-decoration tradition
cards.notes: If your hall participates, leave space for a small surprise on your door and keep gifts and decorations considerate of residence-hall rules.
cards.short_summary: First-year students’ residence-hall doors receive unexpected small gifts and decorations from sophomores.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke identifies Elfing as a first-year and sophomore tradition in which first-year residence-hall doors are unexpectedly decorated with small gifts.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Annual Events | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: A residence-hall tradition involving first-year and sophomore students; follow housing policies and current class guidance.

cards.title: Class Colors and Symbols
cards.subtitle: Class identifiers used at Convocation and other activities
cards.notes: Learn your class color and symbol before major class events, then look for them on banners and other class-related displays.
cards.short_summary: Each class uses a color and symbol as a visible Mount Holyoke identity marker.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke states that, since the early 1900s, classes have used a color and symbol to identify themselves at class-related activities including Convocation.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Annual Events | Mount Holyoke College
cards.access_notes: Class-specific identifiers are used at class-related activities, including Convocation.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Mount Holyoke College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, campus-centered first-weekend sequence with food, nature, study space and ways to begin connecting.

cards.title: Start with a shared dinner
cards.subtitle: Community Center
cards.notes: Use Friday dinner to settle in and compare weekend plans. Confirm service before heading over; published semester hours list Friday and Saturday dinner until midnight.
cards.short_summary: A practical first meet-up point for a Friday arrival.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dining Commons publishes Friday and Saturday semester dinner hours of 5 p.m. to 12 a.m.
cards.source_title: Dining Center Hours and Opening/Closing Schedule
cards.access_notes: Semester hours resume September 6, 2026; Friday and Saturday dinner is listed 5 p.m.–12 a.m. Purchases or a meal plan are required for food.

cards.title: Take the lake loop after breakfast
cards.subtitle: Trailhead near Kendall Sports & Dance Complex
cards.notes: Bring water and follow the one-mile loop around Upper Lake. Start near Kendall and the dam, then pause at the wetland-restoration interpretive sites.
cards.short_summary: A documented one-mile campus nature walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke describes Upper Lake Loop as an approximately one-mile trail whose accessible trailhead is near Kendall Sports & Dance Complex and the dam.
cards.access_notes: The College describes campus trails as available to students and the larger community; use the posted trail map and conditions.

cards.title: Step into the greenhouse
cards.subtitle: Mount Holyoke College Botanic Garden
cards.notes: Visit during published weekend hours and look slowly through the living collection. The greenhouse has tropical, subtropical and temperate plants from around the world.
cards.short_summary: An indoor plant stop with regular visitor hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Botanic Garden lists Saturday–Sunday hours of 1–4 p.m. and says Talcott Greenhouse is open to visitors year-round.
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–4 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday 1–4 p.m.; check for changes before visiting.

cards.title: Make room for a quiet pause
cards.subtitle: Eliot House, top floor
cards.notes: Use the garden and teahouse for reading, sketching or quiet sitting. Visit in the listed public afternoon window rather than assuming open access at other times.
cards.short_summary: A designated contemplative space in Eliot House.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke says Wa-shin-an is open to the campus community and public Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 1–5 p.m. during the academic year.
cards.source_title: Quiet, Contemplative and Spiritual Places on Campus
cards.access_notes: Academic-year public hours listed by the College are Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 1–5 p.m.; use it for quiet contemplative practices.

cards.title: Find a study perch and a game
cards.subtitle: LITS Complex
cards.notes: Walk the floors, locate a comfortable study area, then ask the circulation desk about leisure books, films or card games for a relaxed evening back in the hall.
cards.short_summary: A daytime reset with study and leisure resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Williston’s Circulation Desk lends books, films and equipment, and LITS identifies leisure books, films and card games available through the library.
cards.access_notes: The page lists current weekday Circulation Desk hours; borrowing eligibility and library-building access may vary.

cards.title: Take a café-and-library break
cards.subtitle: Williston Library atrium
cards.notes: Meet in the atrium for a drink or baked good, then decide whether to keep exploring or return to your room. Check dining’s current café hours before going.
cards.short_summary: A named café inside the library atrium.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke identifies Frances Perk café in the Williston Library atrium and lists semester service hours, including weekend hours.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Williston Library atrium; dining directs visitors to its current menu and hours. Food and beverages require purchase.

cards.title: Choose a short hill walk
cards.subtitle: Prospect Hill
cards.notes: Use the trail map to pick the Carriage Way Loop or 1882 Footpath. Stay on marked paths and take the route at a pace that works for your group.
cards.short_summary: A roughly one-mile network with mapped route options.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke lists Prospect Hill Trails as a 1.6 km trail area and describes the Carriage Way Loop and 1882 Footpath as routes on Prospect Hill.
cards.access_notes: Consult the College’s downloadable trail map and use marked routes; conditions and accessibility can vary.

cards.title: Save a longer trail for Sunday
cards.subtitle: Campus trail system
cards.notes: If your group wants more distance, use the mapped Stony Brook and Long Farm loop. Plan daylight, shoes for uneven ground and a clear turnaround time.
cards.short_summary: A mapped 3.2 km option for a longer campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Holyoke lists Stony Brook/Long Farm Loop as a 3.2 km campus trail and describes the trail system as serving recreation and learning.
cards.access_notes: Use the official trail map and check weather and trail conditions before setting out.

cards.title: Locate student-life hubs
cards.subtitle: Community Center
cards.notes: Walk through Blanchard to find the Student Art Gallery, Unity Space and Weissman Student Commons. Note the Student Involvement Office for future club questions.
cards.short_summary: A central building for services, student organizations and gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies Blanchard as part of the Community Center and lists the Student Art Gallery, Unity Space and Weissman Student Commons among its areas.
cards.access_notes: Building access and room availability can change with College operations and scheduled events.

cards.title: Put the museum reopening on your calendar
cards.subtitle: Museum Galleries
cards.notes: After its September reopening, visit the reinstalled collection galleries and choose one work to discuss. Check the museum’s visitor page immediately before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum scheduled to reopen with renovated galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum announces that its new collection galleries open September 8, 2026, and its visitor guidelines state that the museum is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: MHCAM at 150: Our New Collection Galleries
cards.access_notes: The museum’s visitor page says it is closed until Fall 2026; this card applies after the announced September 8 reopening. Verify current access before visiting.
